claim: β3-adrenoceptor (β3-AR) is widely recognized as a canonical β-adrenergic G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) that plays a crucial role in mediating adipose thermogenesis in mice.
source: β3-adrenoceptor (β3-AR) is widely recognized as a canonical β-adrenergic G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) that plays a crucial role in mediating adipose thermogenesis in mice.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about β3-AR's role in adipose thermogenesis in mice.

claim: The limited expression of β3-AR in human adipocytes restricts its clinical application.
source: Nonetheless, the limited expression of β3-AR in human adipocytes restricts its clinical application.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comparison of ADRB3 expression levels in human versus mouse adipose tissue shown in the manuscript.

claim: ADGRA3 is an orphan GPCR that plays a significant role in adipose thermogenesis through its constitutively active effects.
source: Our research findings have demonstrated that the adhesion G-protein-coupled receptor A3 (ADGRA3), an orphan GPCR, plays a significant role in adipose thermogenesis through its constitutively active effects.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by multiple experiments including knockdown and overexpression studies.

claim: ADGRA3 exhibited high expression levels in human adipocytes and mouse brown fat.
source: ADGRA3 exhibited high expression levels in human adipocytes and mouse brown fat.
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 1D-E comparing ADGRA3 expression in different tissues.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in an exacerbated obese phenotype in mice.
source: Furthermore, the knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in an exacerbated obese phenotype and a reduction in the expression of thermogenic markers in mice.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3 showing increased body weight and adipose tissue weight in shAdgra3 mice.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a reduction in the expression of thermogenic markers in mice.
source: Furthermore, the knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in an exacerbated obese phenotype and a reduction in the expression of thermogenic markers in mice.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and Western blot data in Figure 3F-J showing decreased expression of UCP1 and other thermogenic genes.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression activated the adipose thermogenic program in mice without exogenous ligand.
source: Conversely, Adgra3 overexpression activated the adipose thermogenic program and improved metabolic homeostasis in mice without exogenous ligand.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 showing increased thermogenic gene expression and improved metabolic parameters in Adgra3 OE mice.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression improved metabolic homeostasis in mice without exogenous ligand.
source: Conversely, Adgra3 overexpression activated the adipose thermogenic program and improved metabolic homeostasis in mice without exogenous ligand.
evidence: This is supported by glucose tolerance test and insulin tolerance test data in Figure 4L-O.

claim: ADGRA3 facilitates the biogenesis of beige human or mouse adipocytes in vitro.
source: We found that ADGRA3 facilitates the biogenesis of beige human or mouse adipocytes in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro experiments shown in Figures 2 and 8 demonstrating increased UCP1 expression and mitochondrial content.

claim: Hesperetin was identified as a potential agonist of ADGRA3.
source: Moreover, hesperetin was identified as a potential agonist of ADGRA3, capable of inducing adipocyte browning and ameliorating insulin resistance in mice.
evidence: This is supported by screening data from PRESTO-Salsa database and functional assays shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Hesperetin is capable of inducing adipocyte browning in mice.
source: Moreover, hesperetin was identified as a potential agonist of ADGRA3, capable of inducing adipocyte browning and ameliorating insulin resistance in mice.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo data in Figure 7 showing increased thermogenic gene expression in hesperetin-treated mice.

claim: Hesperetin is capable of ameliorating insulin resistance in mice.
source: Moreover, hesperetin was identified as a potential agonist of ADGRA3, capable of inducing adipocyte browning and ameliorating insulin resistance in mice.
evidence: This is supported by insulin tolerance test data in Figure 7L showing improved insulin sensitivity.

claim: The overexpression of constitutively active ADGRA3 can induce adipocyte browning by Gs-PKA-CREB axis.
source: In conclusion, our study demonstrated that the overexpression of constitutively active ADGRA3 or the activation of ADGRA3 by hesperetin can induce adipocyte browning by Gs-PKA-CREB axis.
evidence: This is supported by co-IP experiments and signaling pathway analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The activation of ADGRA3 by hesperetin can induce adipocyte browning by Gs-PKA-CREB axis.
source: In conclusion, our study demonstrated that the overexpression of constitutively active ADGRA3 or the activation of ADGRA3 by hesperetin can induce adipocyte browning by Gs-PKA-CREB axis.
evidence: This is supported by experiments in Figure 6 showing hesperetin-induced cAMP production and PKA-CREB activation.

claim: Since 1975, there has been a substantial increase in the global prevalence of obesity, with the magnitude nearly tripling.
source: Since 1975, there has been a substantial increase in the global prevalence of obesity, with the magnitude nearly tripling. The World Health Organization projects that the prevalence of obesity among adults will exceed 20% by the year 2025 (Organization WH, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization.

claim: The World Health Organization projects that the prevalence of obesity among adults will exceed 20% by the year 2025.
source: The World Health Organization projects that the prevalence of obesity among adults will exceed 20% by the year 2025 (Organization WH, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization.

claim: The management of excessive adiposity poses a paramount economic burden and healthcare predicament.
source: Currently, the management of excessive adiposity poses a paramount economic burden and healthcare predicament (Chu et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: There is a significant association between obesity and an increased vulnerability to type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer.
source: In addition to the detrimental social and psychological implications, a multitude of studies have consistently demonstrated a significant association between obesity and an increased vulnerability to a range of health conditions, such as type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer (Twig et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2016; Hyppönen et al., 2019; Calle, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Activating and maintaining the thermogenesis of beige/brown fat has been shown to be effective in treating obesity and related metabolic disorders in humans.
source: Activating and maintaining the thermogenesis of beige/brown fat has been shown to be effective in treating obesity and related metabolic disorders in humans (Yoneshiro et al., 2013; Finlin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The clinical application of β3-AR has been impeded due to its low expression in human adipocytes and the cardiovascular risks associated with other adrenergic receptors.
source: Regrettably, the clinical application of β3-AR has been impeded due to its low expression in human adipocytes and the cardiovascular risks associated with other adrenergic receptors (Sui et al., 2019; Blondin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are the most prevalent class of drug targets among all drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
source: G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are the most prevalent class of drug targets among all drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). They also play a crucial role in the clinical treatment of obesity (Hauser et al., 2017; Müller et al., 2022; Alba et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: GPCRs play a crucial role in the clinical treatment of obesity.
source: They also play a crucial role in the clinical treatment of obesity (Hauser et al., 2017; Müller et al., 2022; Alba et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ADGRA3 exhibits typical domains found in aGPCRs within its N-terminal extracellular region (ECR), including a leucine-rich repeat (LRR), an immunoglobulin-like domain (Ig), a hormone-binding domain (HBD), and a GAIN domain.
source: ADGRA3 is classified as an orphan adhesion G-protein-coupled receptor (aGPCR) and exhibits the typical domains found in aGPCRs within its N-terminal extracellular region (ECR), including a leucine-rich repeat (LRR), an immunoglobulin-like domain (Ig), a hormone-binding domain (HBD), and a GAIN domain (Nybo et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ADGRA3 was initially discovered as a distinctive indicator of various spermatogonial progenitor cells.
source: ADGRA3 was initially discovered as a distinctive indicator of various spermatogonial progenitor cells (Spiess et al., 2019; Seandel et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: aGPCRs have a conservative mechanism of activation which involves the use of tethered ligands in the GAIN domain.
source: Recent studies have shown that the orphan status of receptors has posed challenges to the study of aGPCRs. However, these studies have also uncovered a conservative mechanism of aGPCR activation, which involves the use of tethered ligands in the GAIN domain (Vizurraga et al., 2020; Hamann et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ADGRA3 has been previously identified as a receptor capable of auto-cleavage.
source: ADGRA3 has been previously identified as a receptor capable of auto-cleavage (Sakurai et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: A genome-wide association study (GWAS) demonstrated a significant correlation between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of ADGRA3 and body weight in chickens.
source: A genome-wide association study (GWAS) demonstrated a significant correlation between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of ADGRA3 and body weight in chickens (Cha et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published GWAS study.

claim: 27 BAT-elevated GPCRs were identified from transcriptome analysis.
source: 27 BAT-elevated GPCRs from transcriptome, 515 very high genes in subcutaneous adipocytes and 462 very high genes in visceral adipocytes from the human protein atlas database were analyzed by using a Venn diagram.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 1C and described in the text.

claim: 515 very high genes in subcutaneous adipocytes were identified from the human protein atlas database.
source: 27 BAT-elevated GPCRs from transcriptome, 515 very high genes in subcutaneous adipocytes and 462 very high genes in visceral adipocytes from the human protein atlas database were analyzed by using a Venn diagram.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 462 very high genes in visceral adipocytes were identified from the human protein atlas database.
source: 27 BAT-elevated GPCRs from transcriptome, 515 very high genes in subcutaneous adipocytes and 462 very high genes in visceral adipocytes from the human protein atlas database were analyzed by using a Venn diagram.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The level of Adgra3 expression in mouse adipose tissue was comparatively lower than that of Adrb3.
source: The findings indicated that the level of Adgra3 expression in mouse adipose tissue (Figure 1D) was comparatively lower than that of Adrb3, the coding gene for β3-AR.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPKM data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In human adipose tissue, ADGRA3 expression was observed to be higher than that of ADRB3.
source: Conversely, in human adipose tissue, ADGRA3 expression was observed to be higher than that of ADRB3 (Figure 1E and F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 1E-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: A HFD had a significant inhibitory effect on the expression of ADGRA3 and UCP1 in iWAT and BAT.
source: The findings of the study demonstrated that a HFD had a significant inhibitory effect on the expression of ADGRA3 and UCP1 in iWAT and BAT, while CL robustly increased the expression of ADGRA3 and UCP1 in iWAT and BAT (Figure 1F-G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1F-G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: CL robustly increased the expression of ADGRA3 and UCP1 in iWAT and BAT.
source: The findings of the study demonstrated that a HFD had a significant inhibitory effect on the expression of ADGRA3 and UCP1 in iWAT and BAT, while CL robustly increased the expression of ADGRA3 and UCP1 in iWAT and BAT (Figure 1F-G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1F-G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: In human subcutaneous fat, there was a moderate positive correlation between the expression level of ADGRA3 and the expression level of UCP1 (R=0.5).
source: Interestingly, in human subcutaneous fat, there was a moderate positive correlation between the expression level of ADGRA3 and the expression level of UCP1 (R=0.5, Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1H using GTEx Portal database data.

claim: The expression level of ADRB3 showed a weak positive correlation with the expression level of UCP1 (R=0.21).
source: On the other hand, the expression level of ADRB3 showed a weak positive correlation with the expression level of UCP1 (R=0.21, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: ADGRA3 is predominantly expressed in adipocytes.
source: The results showed that ADGRA3 is predominantly expressed in adipocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR analysis of SVF and mature adipocytes shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The expression level of ADGRA3 in BAT adipocytes was found to be higher compared to WAT adipocytes.
source: Furthermore, the expression level of ADGRA3 in BAT adipocytes was found to be higher compared to WAT adipocytes (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a decrease in the expression of genes related to thermogenesis and lipolysis.
source: Our findings indicate that the knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a decrease in the expression of genes related to thermogenesis and lipolysis (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Adgra3 knockdown resulted in a decrease in the expression of UCP1.
source: Western blot analysis and Mito-Tracker staining revealed a decrease in the expression of UCP1 (Figure 2B) and a reduction in the number of mitochondria (Figure 2C) following Adgra3 knockdown.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Adgra3 knockdown resulted in a reduction in the number of mitochondria.
source: Western blot analysis and Mito-Tracker staining revealed a decrease in the expression of UCP1 (Figure 2B) and a reduction in the number of mitochondria (Figure 2C) following Adgra3 knockdown.
evidence: This claim is supported by Mito-Tracker staining shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Adgra3 knockdown resulted in a significant increase in the number of lipid droplets and intracellular triglyceride levels.
source: The results revealed a significant increase in the number of lipid droplets and intracellular triglyceride levels (Figure 2C–D) following Adgra3 knockdown.
evidence: This claim is supported by Bodipy staining and triglyceride assay data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The uptake of 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-NBDG) by adipocytes was significantly inhibited following the knockdown of Adgra3.
source: Moreover, the uptake of 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-NBDG), a fluorescently-labeled deoxyglucose analog, by adipocytes was significantly inhibited following the knockdown of Adgra3 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The loss of ADGRA3 decreased the both basal and max OCR of adipocytes.
source: The results indicated that the loss of ADGRA3 decreased the both basal and max OCR of adipocytes (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by oxygen consumption rate measurements shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: The overexpression of Adgra3 resulted in an up-regulation in the expression of UCP1 in 3T3-L1 mature beige-like adipocytes.
source: Following the overexpression of Adgra3, there was an observed up-regulation in the expression of UCP1 in 3T3-L1 mature beige-like adipocytes (Figure 2H–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 2H-I.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression resulted in an increase in the quantity of mitochondria.
source: Additionally, Mito-Tracker staining revealed an increase in the quantity of mitochondria (Figure 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Mito-Tracker staining shown in Figure 2J.

claim: There was a notable reduction observed in the lipid droplets and intracellular triglyceride levels subsequent to the overexpression of Adgra3.
source: There was a notable reduction observed in the lipid droplets and intracellular triglyceride levels (Figure 2J–K) subsequent to the overexpression of Adgra3.
evidence: This claim is supported by Bodipy staining and triglyceride assay data shown in Figure 2J-K.

claim: The overexpression of Adgra3 resulted in an increased uptake of 2-NBDG by adipocytes.
source: Moreover, the findings indicated that the overexpression of Adgra3 resulted in an increased uptake of 2-NBDG by adipocytes (Figure 2L) and increased basal and maximum OCR (Figure 2M–N).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose uptake assay data shown in Figure 2L.

claim: The overexpression of Adgra3 increased basal and maximum OCR.
source: Moreover, the findings indicated that the overexpression of Adgra3 resulted in an increased uptake of 2-NBDG by adipocytes (Figure 2L) and increased basal and maximum OCR (Figure 2M–N).
evidence: This claim is supported by oxygen consumption rate measurements shown in Figure 2M-N.

claim: There was a significant increase in the weight of shAdgra3 mice.
source: After knocking down Adgra3 in mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B), there was a significant increase in the weight of shAdgra3 mice (mice with Adgra3 knockdown; Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Serum triacylglycerol (TG) levels were significantly higher in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Serum triacylglycerol (TG) levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), weight of iWAT, epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) and BAT (Figure 3C) were significantly higher in shAdgra3 mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by serum TG measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Weight of iWAT, epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) and BAT were significantly higher in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Serum triacylglycerol (TG) levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), weight of iWAT, epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) and BAT (Figure 3C) were significantly higher in shAdgra3 mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by tissue weight measurements shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a significant reduction in both body temperature and BAT temperature.
source: Remarkably, the knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a significant reduction in both body temperature (Figure 3D) and BAT temperature (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by temperature measurements shown in Figure 3D-E.

claim: The nanoparticle-mediated Adgra3 knockdown does not exert an inhibitory effect on thyroid activity.
source: Given the crucial influence of thyroid activity on thermogenesis, we measured the levels of serum-free tetraiodothyronine (fT4) to evaluate the consequences of Adgra3 knockdown on thyroid activity, which indicated that the nanoparticle-mediated Adgra3 knockdown does not exert an inhibitory effect on thyroid activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by serum fT4 measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a significant decrease in the expression of genes related to thermogenesis and lipolysis in both iWAT and BAT.
source: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a significant decrease in the expression of genes related to thermogenesis and lipolysis in both iWAT (Figure 3F) and BAT (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3F-G.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in an increase in the size of lipid droplets and a decrease in the number of mitochondria in BAT.
source: Additionally, it was observed that the knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in an increase in the size of lipid droplets and a decrease in the number of mitochondria in BAT (Figure 3K).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy images shown in Figure 3K.

claim: shAdgra3 mice exhibited significant disruptions in overall glycemic homeostasis.
source: Furthermore, it was observed that shAdgra3 mice exhibited significant disruptions in overall glycemic homeostasis (Figure 3L) and insulin sensitivity (Figure 3M).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: shAdgra3 mice exhibited significant disruptions in insulin sensitivity.
source: Furthermore, it was observed that shAdgra3 mice exhibited significant disruptions in overall glycemic homeostasis (Figure 3L) and insulin sensitivity (Figure 3M).
evidence: This claim is supported by insulin tolerance test data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: The fasting serum insulin level was increased in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Moreover, the fasting serum insulin level was increased and the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) showed an increase in shAdgra3 mice (Figure 3N–O).
evidence: This claim is supported by serum insulin measurements shown in Figure 3N.

claim: The homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) showed an increase in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Moreover, the fasting serum insulin level was increased and the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) showed an increase in shAdgra3 mice (Figure 3N–O).
evidence: This claim is supported by HOMA-IR calculations shown in Figure 3O.

claim: The growth of body weight of Adgra3 OE mice was alleviated during the HFD feeding.
source: The growth of body weight of Adgra3 OE mice was alleviated (Figure 4B) during the HFD feeding accompanied with a slight decrease of food intake (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The weight of iWAT, eWAT, BAT, and liver were significantly decreased in Adgra3 OE mice.
source: Furthermore, the weight of iWAT, eWAT, BAT, and liver (Figure 4C) were significantly decreased in Adgra3 OE mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by tissue weight measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The Adgra3 OE mice exhibited an elevation in both body temperature and BAT temperature.
source: The Adgra3 OE mice exhibited an elevation in both body temperature (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) and BAT temperature (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), while there was no difference in serum fT4 levels (Figure 4—figure supplements 1F and 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by temperature measurements shown in Figure 4D-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: There was no difference in serum fT4 levels between Adgra3 OE mice and control mice.
source: The Adgra3 OE mice exhibited an elevation in both body temperature (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) and BAT temperature (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), while there was no difference in serum fT4 levels (Figure 4—figure supplements 1F and 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by serum fT4 measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 1F and 2B.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression decreased the TG level in serum and liver.
source: Meanwhile, Adgra3 overexpression decreased the TG level in serum and liver (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C–D) as well as the area of adipocytes in iWAT, eWAT, BAT, and liver (Figure 4—figure supplements 1G and 2E-F).
evidence: This claim is supported by TG measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C-D.

claim: The expression levels of thermogenic and lipolysis-related genes were elevated in iWAT and BAT after Adgra3 overexpression.
source: Moreover, the expression levels of thermogenic and lipolysis-related genes were elevated in iWAT (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H) and BAT (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4F-G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1H-I.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression improved the glucose homeostasis of HFD mice.
source: The glucose tolerance test (GTT) presented that Adgra3 overexpression improved the glucose homeostasis of HFD mice (Figure 4L).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression alleviated the insulin resistance of HFD mice.
source: The insulin tolerance test (ITT) showed that Adgra3 overexpression alleviated the insulin resistance of HFD mice (Figure 4M).
evidence: This claim is supported by insulin tolerance test data shown in Figure 4M.

claim: The fasting serum insulin level was reduced after Adgra3 overexpression.
source: Moreover, the fasting serum insulin level was reduced after Adgra3 overexpression (Figure 4N) and the HOMA-IR also showed a robust improvement (Figure 4O) in Adgra3OE mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by serum insulin measurements shown in Figure 4N.

claim: The HOMA-IR showed a robust improvement in Adgra3OE mice.
source: Moreover, the fasting serum insulin level was reduced after Adgra3 overexpression (Figure 4N) and the HOMA-IR also showed a robust improvement (Figure 4O) in Adgra3OE mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by HOMA-IR calculations shown in Figure 4O.

claim: Mouse ADGRA3 coupled to the Gs protein.
source: The results of the co-IP experiment demonstrated that mouse ADGRA3 coupled to the Gs protein (Figure 5A–B), while no interaction was observed with the other three Gα proteins (Gi, Gq and G12; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: No interaction was observed between ADGRA3 and Gi, Gq and G12 proteins.
source: The results of the co-IP experiment demonstrated that mouse ADGRA3 coupled to the Gs protein (Figure 5A–B), while no interaction was observed with the other three Gα proteins (Gi, Gq and G12; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: The overexpression of Adgra3 is capable of inducing cAMP production.
source: Hence, the overexpression of Adgra3 is capable of inducing cAMP production (Figure 5C), which serves as a second messenger indicating the activation of downstream signals mediated by Gs protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by cAMP measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The effect of Adgra3 overexpression on cAMP production is dependent on Gs protein.
source: Additionally, our findings indicate that the effect of Adgra3 overexpression on cAMP production is dependent on Gs protein (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by cAMP measurements with Gnas knockdown shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The overexpression of Adgra3 leads to an elevation in the phosphorylated form of CREB (p-CREB).
source: As expected, the Western-blot analysis revealed that the overexpression of Adgra3 leads to an elevation in the phosphorylated form of CREB (p-CREB), indicating an increase in PKA-CREB signaling activity. This effect was observed in 3T3-L1 (Figure 5E), as well as in the iWAT and BAT (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5E-F.

claim: The knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a decrease in the level of p-CREB in 3T3-L1, iWAT and BAT.
source: Consistently, the knockdown of Adgra3 resulted in a decrease in the level of p-CREB in 3T3-L1 (Figure 5G), as well as in iWAT and BAT (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5G-H.

claim: Adgra3 overexpression was found to be adequate in inducing the expression of UCP1 in 3T3-L1 cells, but this effect was observed to be eliminated when Gnas was knocked down.
source: Adgra3 overexpression was found to be adequate in inducing the expression of UCP1 in 3T3-L1 cells. However, this effect was observed to be eliminated when Gnas was knocked down (Figure 5I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: PKAi effectively inhibited the activation of PKA-CREB signaling and UCP1 expression induced by Adgra3 overexpression.
source: The results showed that PKAi effectively inhibited the activation of PKA-CREB signaling and UCP1 expression induced by Adgra3 overexpression (Figure 5J, Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5J and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Hesperetin treatment stimulates cAMP production.
source: The results showed that hesperetin treatment stimulates cAMP production (Figure 6B) and increases the expression level of UCP1 and p-CREB (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by cAMP measurements shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Hesperetin treatment increases the expression level of UCP1 and p-CREB.
source: The results showed that hesperetin treatment stimulates cAMP production (Figure 6B) and increases the expression level of UCP1 and p-CREB (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: The induction effect of hesperetin on UCP1 and p-CREB is eliminated when Adgra3 is knocked down.
source: We found that the induction effect of hesperetin on UCP1 and p-CREB is eliminated when Adgra3 is knocked down (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: Hesperetin increased the both basal and max OCR of adipocytes, which was ADGRA3-dependent.
source: The results indicated that hesperetin increased the both basal and max OCR of adipocytes, which was ADGRA3-dependent (Figure 6G–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by oxygen consumption rate measurements shown in Figure 6G-H.

claim: The induction effect of hesperetin on UCP1 and p-CREB is attenuated after Gnas knocked down.
source: Moreover, the results showed that the induction effect of hesperetin on UCP1 and p-CREB is attenuated after Gnas knocked down (Figure 6I–J), suggesting that hesperetin up-regulates UCP1 and activates PKA-CREB axis dependent on Gs.
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6I-J.

claim: Hesperetin treatment resulted in the upregulation of UCP1 and p-CREB, but this effect was found to be eliminated when PKAi was applied.
source: The results revealed that hesperetin treatment resulted in the upregulation of UCP1 and p-CREB. However, this effect was found to be eliminated when PKAi was applied (Figure 6K–L), suggesting that the induction of UCP1 and p-CREB by hesperetin is dependent on PKA.
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6K-L.

claim: Hesperetin was found to alleviate the growth of body weight during the HFD feeding, which was dependent on ADGRA3.
source: Hesperetin was found to alleviate the growth of body weight (Figure 7B) during the HFD feeding and the weight of iWAT, eWAT, BAT and liver weight ratio (Figure 7C), which was dependent on ADGRA3.
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 7B comparing hesperetin treatment in shNC and shAdgra3 mice.

claim: Hesperetin increased body temperature and BAT temperature in shNC mice, which were significantly blunted in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Hesperetin increased body temperature (Figure 7D) and BAT temperature (Figure 7E) in shNC mice, which were significantly blunted in shAdgra3 mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by temperature measurements shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: Hesperetin treatment does not activate thyroid activity.
source: The levels of serum fT4 were measured to evaluate the consequences of hesperetin treatment on thyroid activity, which indicated that hesperetin treatment does not activate thyroid activity (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by serum fT4 measurements shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Hesperetin induced a decline in TG level in both serum and liver, but these effects were absent in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Concurrently, hesperetin induced a decline in TG level in both serum (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C) and liver (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D), and also reduced the area of adipocytes in iWAT (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E) and BAT (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F). However, these effects were absent in shAdgra3 mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by TG measurements shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: The expression level of UCP1 were elevated in both iWAT and BAT after hesperetin treatment in shNC mice but not in shAdgra3 mice.
source: Moreover, the expression level of UCP1 were elevated in both iWAT (Figure 7F and H) and BAT (Figure 7G and I) after hesperetin treatment in shNC mice but not in shAdgra3 mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7F-I.

claim: Hesperetin improved the glucose resistance of HFD mice which showed no effect in shAdgra3 mice.
source: The GTT presented that hesperetin improved the glucose resistance of HFD mice which showed no effect in shAdgra3 mice (Figure 7K).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 7K.

claim: Hesperetin alleviated the insulin resistance of HFD mice which showed no significance in shAdgra3 mice.
source: The ITT showed that hesperetin alleviated the insulin resistance of HFD mice which showed no significance in shAdgra3 mice (Figure 7L).
evidence: This claim is supported by insulin tolerance test data shown in Figure 7L.

claim: The fasting serum insulin level was reduced after hesperetin treatment, which was dependent on ADGRA3.
source: Moreover, the fasting serum insulin level was reduced after hesperetin treatment (Figure 7M) and the HOMA-IR also showed a moderate improvement (Figure 7N), which were dependent on ADGRA3.
evidence: This claim is supported by serum insulin measurements shown in Figure 7M.

claim: The HOMA-IR showed a moderate improvement after hesperetin treatment, which was dependent on ADGRA3.
source: Moreover, the fasting serum insulin level was reduced after hesperetin treatment (Figure 7M) and the HOMA-IR also showed a moderate improvement (Figure 7N), which were dependent on ADGRA3.
evidence: This claim is supported by HOMA-IR calculations shown in Figure 7N.

claim: ADGRA3 knockdown led to a diminished expression of UCP1 in human adipocytes.
source: The results showed that ADGRA3 knockdown led to a diminished expression of UCP1 (Figure 8A and E), whereas its overexpression elicited an enhancement in UCP1 expression (Figure 8B and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8A and E.

claim: ADGRA3 overexpression elicited an enhancement in UCP1 expression in human adipocytes.
source: The results showed that ADGRA3 knockdown led to a diminished expression of UCP1 (Figure 8A and E), whereas its overexpression elicited an enhancement in UCP1 expression (Figure 8B and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8B and F.

claim: ADGRA3 knockdown resulted in a notable increase in lipid droplet count accompanied by a decrease in mitochondrial number in human adipocytes.
source: Furthermore, Mito-Tracker and lipid droplet fluorescence staining illuminated a notable increase in lipid droplet count accompanied by a decrease in mitochondrial number following ADGRA3 knockdown (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence staining data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: ADGRA3 overexpression resulted in a visible surge in mitochondrial quantity and a marked reduction in lipid droplet presence in human adipocytes.
source: Conversely, ADGRA3 overexpression resulted in a visible surge in mitochondrial quantity and a marked reduction in lipid droplet presence (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence staining data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The induction effect of hesperetin on UCP1 is eliminated when Adgra3 is knocked down in mouse primary adipocytes.
source: To further verify whether hesperetin induces the expression of UCP1 via ADGRA3, we treated mouse primary adipocytes with hesperetin and shAdgra3, respectively. We found that the induction effect of hesperetin on UCP1 is eliminated when Adgra3 is knocked down (Figure 8G–H) in primary cultures.
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8G-H.

claim: Treatment with the chronic β3-AR agonist mirabegron leads to an increase in human brown fat, HDL cholesterol, and insulin sensitivity.
source: A clinical trial revealed that treatment with the chronic β3-AR agonist mirabegron leads to an increase in human brown fat, HDL cholesterol, and insulin sensitivity (O'Mara et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a clinical trial.

claim: Oral administration of mirabegron only elicits an increase in BAT thermogenesis when administered at the maximal allowable dose.
source: Subsequently, Blondin et al discovered that oral administration of mirabegron only elicits an increase in BAT thermogenesis when administered at the maximal allowable dose, indicating that human brown adipocyte thermogenesis is primarily driven by β2-adrenoceptor (β2-AR) stimulation (Blondin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Human brown adipocyte thermogenesis is primarily driven by β2-adrenoceptor (β2-AR) stimulation.
source: Subsequently, Blondin et al discovered that oral administration of mirabegron only elicits an increase in BAT thermogenesis when administered at the maximal allowable dose, indicating that human brown adipocyte thermogenesis is primarily driven by β2-adrenoceptor (β2-AR) stimulation (Blondin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Much higher levels of ADRB2 expression were found in human white adipose tissue than ADRB3.
source: Consistent with this finding, we found much higher levels of ADRB2 expression in human white adipose tissue than ADRB3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Simultaneous activation of β2-AR and β3-AR enhances whole-body metabolism through beneficial effects on skeletal muscle and BAT.
source: Furthermore, a recent study has demonstrated that simultaneous activation of β2-AR and β3-AR enhances whole-body metabolism through beneficial effects on skeletal muscle and BAT (Talamonti et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The promotion of thermogenesis in brown and beige adipocytes in rodents was effectively achieved by the β3-adrenoceptor agonist.
source: While the promotion of thermogenesis in brown and beige adipocytes in rodents was effectively achieved by the β3-adrenoceptor agonist, the clinical implications of this finding appear to be unfeasible in humans due to the low efficacy of β3-adrenoceptor agonists (Fisher et al., 2012; Kajimura et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The clinical implications of β3-adrenoceptor agonists appear to be unfeasible in humans due to the low efficacy of β3-adrenoceptor agonists.
source: While the promotion of thermogenesis in brown and beige adipocytes in rodents was effectively achieved by the β3-adrenoceptor agonist, the clinical implications of this finding appear to be unfeasible in humans due to the low efficacy of β3-adrenoceptor agonists (Fisher et al., 2012; Kajimura et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ADRB2 plays a pivotal role in bronchodilation and vasodilation.
source: Nevertheless, given ADRB2's pivotal role in bronchodilation and vasodilation (Hizawa, 2011; Morell et al., 2021), we believe that ADGRA3 has the potential to be an alternative target for inducing adipose thermogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Hesperetin has been reported to attenuate the age-related metabolic decline, reduce fat and improve glucose homeostasis in naturally aged mice.
source: Hesperetin has been reported to attenuate the age-related metabolic decline, reduce fat and improve glucose homeostasis in naturally aged mice (Yeh et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Previous studies showed that hesperetin improved glycemic control.
source: Previous studies showed that hesperetin improved glycemic control (Yeh et al., 2022; Xue et al., 2016) and was involved in adipocyte differentiation (Subash-Babu and Alshatwi, 2015), but whether hesperetin induces the biogenesis of beige adipocyte was uncertain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Hesperetin was involved in adipocyte differentiation.
source: Previous studies showed that hesperetin improved glycemic control (Yeh et al., 2022; Xue et al., 2016) and was involved in adipocyte differentiation (Subash-Babu and Alshatwi, 2015), but whether hesperetin induces the biogenesis of beige adipocyte was uncertain.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Male mice deficient in ADGRA3 showed obstructive azoospermia with high penetrance.
source: In previous reports, male mice deficient in ADGRA3 showed obstructive azoospermia with high penetrance (Nybo et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The induction of beige fat has been investigated as a potentially effective therapeutic approach in combating obesity.
source: The induction of beige fat has been investigated as a potentially effective therapeutic approach in combating obesity (Harms and Seale, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ADGRA3 is a GPCR that exhibits high expression in human adipocytes.
source: In this study, we have identified ADGRA3 as a novel GPCR therapeutic target that exhibits high expression in human adipocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by expression data in Figure 1.

claim: In human adipose tissue, ADGRA3 is expressed at a lower level than ADRB2.
source: In human adipose tissue, ADGRA3 is expressed at a lower level than ADRB2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 E), which has been shown to be the main receptor mediating adrenergic activation of thermogenesis in human brown adipocytes (Blondin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and a citation.

claim: ADRB2 has been shown to be the main receptor mediating adrenergic activation of thermogenesis in human brown adipocytes.
source: In human adipose tissue, ADGRA3 is expressed at a lower level than ADRB2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 E), which has been shown to be the main receptor mediating adrenergic activation of thermogenesis in human brown adipocytes (Blondin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: The non-targeted nanoparticle approach utilized in this study for modulating Adgra3 expression levels in vivo alter Adgra3 expression in tissues beyond adipose tissue.
source: Given the consideration that the non-targeted nanoparticle approach utilized in this study for modulating Adgra3 expression levels in vivo alter Adgra3 expression in tissues beyond adipose tissue (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C), notably the liver and skeletal muscle, the construction of Adgra3 adipose tissue-specific knockout/overexpression mouse models is imperative for a more nuanced understanding of the precise mechanisms underlying the influence of on adipose thermogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data in multiple tissues shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: The observed decrease in TG levels in both serum and liver might be attributed to the significant increase in Adgra3 expression in the liver.
source: Furthermore, it is crucial to highlight that the observed decrease in TG levels in both serum and liver (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C–D) might be attributed to the significant increase in Adgra3 expression in the liver, which is a consequence of the nanoparticle-mediated overexpression of Adgra3.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between liver Adgra3 expression and TG levels.
